preamble: Vocalization of the tap [ɾ] to the open vowel [a] after a vowel. In most Tarifit (Riffian Berber) varieties of northern Morocco, original *r, a tap, is vocalized when it follows a vowel and does not precede one. After /i/ and /u/ it surfaces as [a] and lowers the preceding vowel, so /iɾ/ is realized [ɛa] and /uɾ/ [ɔa] (ssird 'to wash' [sːɛað], uyur 'to walk' [ʊjɔa]); after /a/ only a single vowel [a ~ æ] remains (zemmar 'to be able to' [zəmːa ~ æ]). Before a vowel the tap is kept (tamara 'hard work, misery'). The easternmost dialects (Icebdanen, Iznasen) and those west of Ayt Waayaɣeř do not vocalize. German and Danish vocalize their uvular rhotic to [ɐ] in the same coda position.

languageExamples.context: After a vowel, before a consonant or word-finally

examples.note: /iɾ/ is realized [ɛa]: the tap becomes [a] and /i/ is lowered.

Wikipedia's example of the vocalization (written taddaat); its table gives /aɾ/ as a single vowel [a ~ æ] (zemmar 'to be able to' [zəmːa ~ æ]), so after /a/ vocalization and loss cannot be told apart.
